newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No deadline for end to Brazil Santos strike - union.
newsitem.headline: No deadline for end to Brazil Santos strike - union.

text.p: A strike by administrative portworkers at Brazil's port of Santos will continue indefinitely while unions try to seal a new collective wage agreement with the port, a union spokesman said.
"In order to operate 24 hours in six-hour turns, we need to negotiate a new collective wage agreement," said Francisco Luiz Bertozzi, vice-president of the Administrative Portworkers' Union.
This meant there was no forecast for an end to the dispute, which depends on negotiations currently taking place at the local division of the Labor Ministry, he said.
The strike, which began at 0100 local/0400 GMT, has partially paralyzed the port and halted loading of sugar and soybeans, the port authority CODESP said.

The workers are protesting against not being consulted about the port's switch to 24-hour operations, due to have begun on June 30 and aimed at speeding the transit of cargoes and creating cost savings for users.
"We workers are not against the 24-hour (operation of the) port," Bertozzi said. "But we have a rotation system, a work system that this completely upsets."
"It could be that after a judgement, we'll go back to work," he said. Asked if this could happen today, he replied, "I think it's going to be pretty hard, if not impossible."
The strike would continue indefinitely with administrative portworkers holding an assembly at 1700 local/2000 GMT every day to review the situation, Bertozzi said.
There were two separate round table discussions currently going on at the Labor Ministry offices, one on wages and another on 24-hour operations, he said.
The unions involve CODESP and four unions representing administrative workers, port operators, motorway workers and crane operators, a port spokeswoman said.

While other unions were not taking part in the strike, they are still operating under the old system of eight-hour shifts, meaning that the port would effectively not be able to switch to 24-hour operation, he said. ((--Joelle Diderich, Sao Paulo newsroom +55 11 248 5417))
